Hi Marco / Lena / Yara,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand FinPay's priorities and constraints. Quick recap and proposed mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align on owners and dates.

Stakeholder map (from call)
- Marco Ruiz — CFO / Economic buyer (decision target: EOM June)
- Lena Torres — Head of Engineering (tech evaluation, perf/latency)
- Yara Haddad — Head of Security/InfoSec (SOC2, data residency, auditability)
- Sasha Patel — Procurement (contracts, PO, legal redlines)

Key decision criteria you shared
- 99th percentile latency under 150ms for core inference path
- Unit cost < $0.003/token equivalent for peak workloads
- SOC2 Type II + DPA, support for US data residency
- Predictable capacity / ability to burst for month-end processing windows

Proposed MAP (milestones & owners)
1) Technical deep-dive (SE demo + perf runbook) — owner: Avery Johnson (Redwood) / Lena (FinPay) — target: 2026-06-02
2) Security evidence & DPA review — owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Yara (FinPay) — target: 2026-06-03 (SOC2 summary attached)
3) Pricing & commercial proposal — owner: Marissa (Redwood) / Marco (FinPay) — target: 2026-06-03
4) Contract review & redlines (SPLA/DPA) — owner: Sasha (FinPay) / Legal (Redwood) — target: 2026-06-10
5) Decision & PO issuance — owner: Marco / Sasha — target: 2026-06-30

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.pdf (high-level MAP / timeline) — I've attached a first-pass that reflects what we discussed.

Next steps for this thread
- Can you confirm the stakeholder list and the proposed dates (especially the 6/2 tech deep-dive)?
- Sasha, if you can confirm procurement timeline/process that would be great — are there standard form requirements (e.g., SOC2 report, certificate, DPA template)?

Happy to adjust — we'll keep this MAP living in the shared Drive link (below) and iterate.

Thanks!

— Marissa Cole
